newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour lead has dropped, poll says. [CORRECTED 07:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: UK Labour lead has dropped, poll says. [CORRECTED 07:35 GMT]

text.p: The opposition Labour Party's lead over Britain's ruling Conservatives has fallen to its lowest level for three years, according to an opinion poll in Thursday's Guardian newspaper.

The ICM poll put Labour on 47 percent, down five points from a poll by the same company last month, with the Conservatives up three at 34 percent and the Liberal Democrats (corrects party name) down one at 15 percent.

The findings will be welcomed by Conservative Party strategists, who had predicted a resurgence in support in the run-up to the next general election, which Prime Minister John Major must call by next May.

Polls carried out by other companies have given Labour a lead of up to 28 points, but ICM said it thought Conservative supporters were reluctant to admit how they would really vote and had adjusted its poll findings accordingly.
ICM interviewed 1,202 people across Britain by telephone on November 1 and 2.
